Puts it on a fuller length around off, Stoneman pushes it back from the inner half of the bat.
Change of angle from Gabriel. He attempts a yorker but ends up serving a full toss on middle, Mark easily flicks it through mid-wicket and gathers a couple of runs.
Full and wide outside off, Stoneman allows it through.
Shannon Gabriel is into the attack.
Joe Root is the next man in.

OUT! The missed chance has not cost them a lot. Westley is walking back. Holder, captain fantastic gets his second. Dishes out a full ball outside off, inviting Tom to go after it and he does with an expansive drive. The ball takes the edge and goes to Dowrich who grabs it easily. The players appeal and the umpire gives it out. A needless shot by Westley there, he could have easily left it. Second wicket down for England and they are still 88 runs behind.
Length on off, Westley defends it off the front foot.
Bowls it wide outside off, Westley does not play at it.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Back of a length outside off, Westley guides it towards third man. The fielder from gully hares after it and does well to field it but makes a meal out of it while throwing. The batsmen take two.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

CONFUSION BUT SAFE IN THE END! Fuller outside off, Stoneman drives it through covers and completes a run. Mark sets off for the second run but Westley is ball-watching. He almost reaches the other end and then Westley sets off. Gabriel in the deep does well to get to the ball by running to his left but returns a wayward throw at the bowler's end. Bishoo fails to collect it but recovers well. He then has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses. Westley who was half-way down the pitch makes his ground. A chance goes abegging. Bishoo should have remained calm there. Maybe, he got too excited.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Edged but short! Tosses it up on off, Stoneman tries to defend but gets an outside edge which falls short of first slip.

Drags his length back outside off, turns back in. Stoneman makes room and cuts it behind point. They run one and set off for the second run. Gabriel is quick to the ball and fires a throw to the keeper who whips the bails off in a flash but Mark has made his ground.
Flatter outside off, Stoneman opts not to play at it.
Starts off with a full delivery outside off, Stoneman drives it through covers for a couple.
Finally, Devendra Bishoo gets the ball in his hand.
Lovely shot! Fuller on off, Westley times his drive straight back down the ground. The fielder from mid off gives it a chase and keeps it down to two.
Length outside off, Westley lets it through to the keeper.
Nice inswing for Holder but it makes the shot easier for Stoneman. Fuller in length drifting onto the pads, Stoneman flicks it through square leg for a run.
Stoneman has been hit on his hand and looks in a lot of pain here. The physio is out there to have a look. Some swelling on his little finger.

That has come back in a long, long way. Shorter in length outside off, jags back in sharply and bounces more than expected. Stoneman tries to block it off the back foot but is surprised by the movement and bounce. He is late onto the shot and the ball hits him on the bottom hand. That must have hurt him.
Just short of a length around middle, moves away off the deck. Stoneman tries to defend but gets it off the outer half to gully.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stoneman does not fiddle with it.
The men concerned are out in the middle. Westley and Stoneman will continue their innings. Jason Holder will continue his spell.
...Day 3, Session 3...

A session which finally belongs to England. They started off the session being 169 runs behind and  have cut it down to 101 runs with the loss of only one wicket. It was a brilliant start for them  with the two opening batsmen stitching a partnership of 58 before Jason Holder provided the breakthrough. He was excellent with the ball and got his reward in the wicket of Alastair Cook. Westley has come out and looked solid but there is assistance from the wicket for the bowlers. England will hope these two surge a good partnership and take England close to the lead. Whereas, the visitors would hope to keep chipping away at the wickets after the break. Join us for the final session in a while.
Length ball outside off, Westley is in no mood to play at it. TEA ON DAY 3!
Comes steaming in and bowls a full ball on leg stump, almost a yorker. Stoneman does well to flick it down to fine leg for a run.
Comes from around the wicket and fires it on the stumps. Stoneman plays it with the angle towards mid on.
WIDE! Very wide outside off, Stoneman need not play at it and the umpire signals a wide.
Back of a length on off, Mark guides it to point.

NOT OUT! West Indies lose a review. Not a bad review though, looked close to the naked eye. Lands it on a length around leg stump. Stoneman misses the flick and is rapped on the pads. The Windies go up but the umpire shakes his head. Gabriel wants it to be reviewed and Holder obliges. They go upstairs. Replays show there was no inside edge but the ball had pitched outside leg. The decision stands.
A review for an lbw has been taken against Stoneman. It looks close.
FOUR! Lucky boundary! Back of a length on off, Stoneman tries to force it through the off side but gets an outside edge through the slip cordon for a boundary.
Good length on off, Westley lunges forward and defends it.
Length around off, nips back in. Westley watchfully lets it through to the keeper. A good leave in the end. That came back in sharply.
Good length around off, Westley keeps his eyes on the ball and leaves it.
Shorter outside off, Tom goes for the pull but is beaten by the low bounce.
Sprays it down the leg side, Westley misses the flick and the ball goes to the keeper.
Fuller outside off, Westley opts not to play at it.
Slower through the air but wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
A straighter one on the stumps, Stoneman prods forward and defends it.
Fires it outside off, Stoneman does not play at it.
Shorter in length on off, turning back in. Westley camps back and flicks it through square leg for a run.
Flatter on off, Westley lunges forward and blocks it.
Darts it on the pads, Westley shuffles across and flicks it behind square on the leg side for a run.
Shorter in length on the pads of the batsman. Westley tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads as the ball rolls towards square leg. The batsmen take a run.
A touch fuller in length on off, the batsman drives it back to the bowler.
Good length outside off, Westley opts not to play at it.
Bowls it outside off, Tom watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
Good length on off, Westley defends it off the front foot.
Every ball is moving off the seam! Length ball around off, nips away. Westley tries to defend it but gets beaten.
Fuller outside off, Stoneman eases it to covers. Back-to-back maidens.
Bowls it outside off, Stoneman does not play at it.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
This one turns and bounces! Slower through the air on off, turning away. Stoneman tries to defend but gets beaten.
That has stayed low! Flatter outside off, Stoneman lets it through to the keeper. The ball stays very low. Dowrich does well to collect it.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through. A maiden wicket for Holder brilliant.
Tom Westley is the next man in.

OUT! The Windies skipper strikes! He deserves the wicket. He has been explicable with his lines and lengths. He beat the outside edge of Cook thrice in this over and finally gets him to nick one. Lands it on a length around off and moves away ever-so-slightly. Cook has to play at it, pokes inside the line and gets an outside edge to the keeper who gobbles it. They all go up and the umpire gives it out. Holder is ecstatic and why wouldn't he be? He has got the big fish. Cook is walking back and England still trail by another 111 runs.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Three in a row! Lovely bowling from Holder. Good length around off, moves away off the deck. Cook has to play at it as he tries to defend but gets beaten by the away movement.

Beaten again! Length outside off, Cook needlessly pushes at it and gets beaten. The bowler gets excited but nothing from the umpire. there was a sound as it passes the bat but Ultra Edge shows no spike.
Almost an edge! Top bowling from Holder. Length ball around off, nips away off the deck. Cook tries to defend it off the back foot but gets beaten.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
FOUR! Fires it down the leg side, Stoneman gets it fine down the leg side for a boundary. He is going along well here.
Bowls an arm ball on middle, Cook tries to defend but gets it off the inner half past short leg for a run.
Flatter on middle, Cook defends it nicely.
Tosses it up on middle, Cook drives it back to the bowler.
Bowls it on a length around off, Stoneman defends it solidly. A maiden over for Holder.
A tad fuller outside off, Mark opts not to play at it.
Back of a length angling into the batsman. Stoneman defends it to mid on.
Good length on the stumps, Stoneman crouches low and defends it.
Lands it on a length around off, Stoneman gets forward and blocks it.
Fuller outside off, Stoneman drives it to the man at covers
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Full outside off, Cook times it beautifully through the covers. The sweeper in the deep does well to stop the ball and the batsmen run two.
Quicker on off, Cook gets his bat ahead of his pads and defends it.
Fires it on leg stump, Stoneman works it towards square leg for a run.
Flatter on off, goes straight on with the arm. Stoneman covers the line and defends it.
TURN AND BOUNCE! Tosses it outside off, turns away sharply and also gets it to bounce. Stoneman pokes at it and is beaten.

Holder comes around the wicket for the last ball. He bowls it on a length around off, gets it to straighten a touch. Cook is squared up in his defense and it takes the outside edge to gully. Doesn't carry to the fielder.
Good length on off, Cook lunges forward in defense but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket for a brace.
A touch fuller outside off, Cook eases it to point.
Hits the perfect length around off, Cook prods forward and defends it.
Full and wide outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Back of a length on off, Cook defends it watchfully.

FOUR! STREAKY! There were two slips in place but it evades both of them. Fuller outside off, turning away. Stoneman tries to drive it through covers but gets an outside edge through gully and the ball races to the fence.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Drags his length back outside off, Cook cuts it through point for a run.

FOUR! He loves this shot! Flatter outside off, turning away. Cook opens the face of the bat and guides it through short third man. The fielder from point gives it a chase and puts in a dive but all in vain as the ball crosses the ropes.
Bowls it outside off and it turns even more. Cook is in no mood to play at it.
Short and just outside off, Cook camps back and chops it to point.
A touch fuller around off, Stoneman defends it solidly.
Length outside off, Mark guides it to the gully fielder.
Good length on off, Stoneman prods forward and defends it towards cover.
Drifts it on the pads, Cook nudges it down to fine leg for a run.
Close shave! Good length on off, angling away. Cook pokes at it and gets beaten. There is a muted appeal from them but the umpire stays put.
Length outside off, Cook leaves it.
Wide outside off, Stoneman does not fiddle with it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Quicker on off, turning away. Stoneman lunges forward in defense but gets an outside edge to backward point.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Flatter outside off, Stoneman does not play at it.
Almost! Slower through the air on middle, turning away. Cook tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge through cover-point for a run. A risky shot on a turning wicket.
Back of a length on middle, Cook flicks it towards mid-wicket and keeps strike for the next over.
Length outside off, Cook watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
FOUR! Easy for Cook! Short and wide outside off, Cook waits for it to come close and then cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Just ahead of a length outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Fuller and outside off, Cook lets it be.
Good length on off, Cook defends it off the back foot towards covers.
Time for Drinks.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
BEATEN! Lovely stuff! Slower through the air on off, turning away from the left-hander. He pokes at it but gets beaten.
Quicker outside off, turning away. No need for Stoneman to play at it.
Bowls it full outside off, Cook drives it through covers for a run.
Flatter and fuller on the stumps, Cook guides it to point.
Tosses it up on off, Cook drives it to mid off.
Inswinger this time on middle, MS camps back and defends it.
Very well bowled! Bowls it in the channel of uncertainty. Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through. That was good cricket all-around, good ball and it was equally well played.
A touch fuller outside off, Mark watchfully leaves it.
Back of a length outside off, Stoneman does not bother to play at it.
Fuller outside off, Cook times it towards cover-point where the fielder runs to his right and makes a good stop. A single taken.
Length outside off, Cook lets it through to the keeper.
Fires it outside off, turning away. Mark shoulders his arms to it.
Quicker on a length outside off, Stoneman does not need to play at it.
Fuller outside off, Cook leans into it and drives it through covers for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Cook defends it solidly.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Flatter on middle, turning away. Cook rocks back and defends it.
Time for some spin! Roston Chase is into the attack.
Good length outside off, no need for Mark to play at it. A good over by the West Indian skipper.
Length just outside off, Stoneman does not play at it.
A tad fuller outside off, just not there for the drive. Mark still tries to and gets beaten.
Good delivery! Length ball pitched on middle, swinging away. Stoneman tries to defend but gets beaten.
Length ball outside off, Stoneman watches the ball till the end and leaves it.
Length ball outside off, Stoneman does not fiddle with it.
Jason Holder is now into the attack. He has two slips and a gully.
Good length outside off, Cook lets it be.
Goes for the yorker but ends up being a very full ball on off. Cook jams it out.
Fuller outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.

Fuller in length outside off, Stoneman drives it through extra cover. Holder first thinks to dive and stop the ball but then does not. He and Blackwood from covers give it a chase and the latter stops it before the ball crosses the fence. Three taken by the batsmen.
Length ball way outside off, Stoneman watches the ball and leaves it.
Bouncer on leg stump. Cook pulls it down to backward square leg for a run.
Back of a length on middle, Stoneman camps back and defends it.
Length on off, Stoneman defends it solidly.
He has bowled one down the leg side and the other one way outside off. Full and outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it.
Drifts it on the pads, Stoneman fails to clip it and it goes off the pads to the keeper.
Bowls it from wide of the crease and hurls a full ball outside off. Stoneman is in no mood to play at it.
Wayward delivery! Short and down the leg side. Stoneman lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length outside off, Cook points his bat skywards and lets it through.
Length ball angling across the batsman outside off. Cook first thinks of playing at it but then drags his bat out of the way.
A better line! Good length just outside off, Cook keeps his eyes on the ball and leaves it. That was a well-judged leave.
Fuller in length outside off, Stoneman tries to drive it but gets an inside edge down to fine leg for a run.
NO BALL! Again he has overstepped. Bouncer on off, Stoneman plays inside the line and lets it through to the keeper. The umpires are also alert now in calling him for any overstepping.
Lands it on a length outside off, Mark shoulders his arms to it.
Shorter in length on middle, gets big on the batsman. Stoneman does well to keep it down. He takes one hand off as he defends it.
NO BALL! Bangs in a short one on the body of the batsman. Stoneman tucks it towards backward square leg. He has overstepped again.
Bowls it even wider outside off, Cook does not need to play at that one. Has to make the batsman play more, the bowler.
Three balls in a row bowled outside off. Cook is in no mood to play at it. Have to start creeping closer to the off stump line inch by inch.
Fullish length but outside off, Cook plants his front foot forward and lets it be.
Just ahead of a length outside off, Cook has nothing to do with it.
Good length on middle, Cook watchfully defends it back to the bowler.
Fuller in length around off, swinging back in. Cook lunges forward and defends it.
Slips a length ball down the leg side, Stoneman tries to flick but misses.
Length ball on middle, hurrying onto the batsman, Stoneman defends it out to mid-wicket.

Wayward delivery. Short and wide outside off, an easy leave for Stoneman. Called a no ball for overstepping. Gabriel's perennial problem seems to be returning. He didn't bowl a single no ball in the first innings though.
Back of a length ball on leg, angling away towards off, Stoneman goes on his toes and defends it back to the bowler.
Sliding down the leg side, Cook fails to flick and it goes off his pads to the keeper. Dowrich dives to his right but fails to collect the ball. They cross and it's given as a leg bye.
Good length delivery on off, Cook watches the line closely and then trusts the bounce to leave it alone.
Bowls it outside off, Cook has nothing to do with it.
Too wide outside off, Stoneman leaves it unplayed. 14 from the over!

FOUR! This is poor bowling by Roach. He is pitching it up to gain some movement but it ain't there. Stoneman cashes in on another boundary, this time by playing a square drive. He does well to open the face of the bat at the right time to find the gap at backward point.
In the corridor, Stoneman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Wow, growing in confidence. Another half-volley by Roach, around off and Stoneman plays it with a straight bat. Caresses it down the ground through mid off for a glorious boundary.
FOUR! Confidence booster for Stoneman! Roach overpitches it outside off and Stoneman unfurls a sublime extra cover drive for a boundary.
Roach bowls it too straight, angling into the batsman, Stoneman eases it off his pads to deep backward square leg for a couple.

Shortish and around leg, Stoneman fails to work it around and it goes off his thigh pad to fine leg. They cross and a delayed signal from the umpire for a leg bye. That was a huge no ball which was not spotted. Hmmm...

Good length delivery on middle and off, Stoneman plays it down from the crease and pushes it with nice timing through point. Blackwood chases it down just before the rope and they take a couple of runs.
Dishes out a length ball in the zone outside off, Stoneman lifts his bat skywards and allows it through to the keeper.
Fuller length ball on middle and off, Mark gets behind the line in defense.
Too full in length on middle, Stoneman plays an on drive and the mid on fielder dives to make a partial stop. Parries it towards mid off, no run taken.
Good length ball outside off, shaping away from the batsman, Stoneman leaves it alone.
Very full this time, outside off, not much swing, Cook is not tempted by the prospect of playing a cover drive. A watchful leave to end the over.
Roach angles in a full ball on off, Stoneman leans forward, closes the face of the bat and helps it to mid-wicket for a run.
On a length outside off, Stoneman remains back and taps it down to point.
Beauty from Roach! Gets his line right and bowls a length ball just outside off. A hint of away movement there to beat the bat of Stoneman needlessly hanging outside off.
That's a great take by Dowrich, flying to his right. Roach loses his radar and sprays a full ball down the leg side, Stoneman fails to flick and Shane dives full length to collect the ball.
A loosener, wide outside off, from around the wicket, Stoneman leaves it alone.

Kemar Roach to share the new cherry from the other end. He was absolutely brilliant in the first innings and would look to repeat the same heroics. Also, he will hope that his fielders will hold on to the catches coming their way.
Better line, around middle and off, angling away, Cook stays back inside the crease and leaves it alone.
A leg stump line delivery, on a length, Cook tucks it off his pads and plays it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Hurls one across the southpaw, Cook covers the line and shoulders arms.

Edged but safe! A good length ball on this occasion, around middle and moving away to open the batsman in defense. Cook ends up playing at it with soft hands and as a result the edge doesn't carry to the slip cordon.
Tries tempting the batsman by bowling a driving length outside off, Cook allows it through to the keeper.
Stifled appeal for an lbw to start the action. Full and pitching outside leg, Cook fails to flick and it hits him on the pads. The bowler gets excited but the umpire is not interested.
